_doc: Category-30 (Culinary Oils and Fats) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-cat30.mjs — HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Numbers come ONLY from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, selected per subcategory by explicit scope regex, strictest across jurisdictions, at FACE VALUE (no reconstitution — an oil is not reconstituted). Pb/Cd/tAs/iAs/tHg are directly regulated for edible oils (EU 2023/915, Codex named-vegetable-oils, GSO 193:2021, Thailand MOPH 414/2020, Singapore Food Regs 2026, India FSSAI 2016, Israel FCS 2016). No government sets an oil ML for Ni/Cr/Cr-VI/Sn/Al, so each of those cells carries a NUMERIC read-across to the nearest applicable sovereign instrument, disclosed as a read-across (never as direct oil governance): Ni <- EU 2024/1987 formula-liquid 100 (nearest sovereign Ni ML on the matching liquid basis; the more-permissive fruiting-veg 400 was rejected because it would admit literature-flagged-contaminated oil); Cr(total) <- China GB2762 liquid-milk 300 (strictest food total-Cr, matching liquid basis); Cr-VI <- California SWRCB drinking-water MCL 10 (strictest oral-intake Cr-VI; a feasibility-set enforceable limit adopted as a conservative species ceiling, sitting far below the total-Cr screen; in a lipid matrix Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) and is caught by reflex speciation); Sn <- EU 2023/915 canned-food inorganic-tin 200000 (the tin pathway in a bottled oil is packaging migration); Al <- EU 10/2011 aluminium migration limit 1000 (the aluminium pathway in a bottled oil is packaging migration; the specific-migration limit is applied at face value as a conservative total-content ceiling). MeHg is bounded by the binding total-mercury ceiling (MeHg <= tHg by identity; no aquatic methylation pathway in a plant oil and no sovereign MeHg oil limit). Every one of the 11 panel cells therefore terminates in a testable numeric ceiling — firm or bounded-by-parent-total — with a register-verified basis; there are no null control/not-material cells (founder rule 2026-08-25: a category is not finished until every analyte carries a specified limit). The honey-Pb near-miss failure mode remains structurally impossible: the audit pass scans every oil-scoped register row for each analyte every build, and there is no oil-scoped government row for Ni/Cr/Cr-VI/Sn/Al anywhere, so each read-across is audit-clean. No occurrence percentiles are computed.

olive-oil.name: Olive oil (virgin, refined, pomace)
olive-oil.audit_scope: edible fats and oils|edible oils and fats|fats, oils|fats and oils|vegetable oil|named vegetable|named animal fat|olive oil|olive pomace|olive residue|cooking oil|coconut oil|avocado oil|sesame oil|sunflower oil|palm oil|groundnut oil|canola oil|rapeseed oil|fat spread

MeHg.label: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg by identity). A pressed or extracted plant oil has no aquatic methylation pathway and no government sets a methylmercury oil limit, so no independent MeHg source exists; the cell is bounded by the binding total-mercury ceiling (Israel FCS fats and oils, 20 ug/kg); total mercury is measured on every lot and methylmercury is speciated only on a total-mercury exceedance.

Ni.label: No government sets a nickel maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. This reads across the nearest applicable sovereign nickel ML on olive oil's own product-as-placed-on-market (liquid) basis: EU Reg 2024/1987 nickel in infant and young-child formula (liquid form), 100 ug/kg. The more permissive EU fruiting-vegetable nickel ML (400 ug/kg) was the alternative food-type sibling; it was rejected because it would admit oil at concentrations the primary literature flags as contaminated (ground-harvest samples reported at 220-330 ug/kg). Disclosed as a read-across, not direct EU governance of oil; clean commercial olive oil clears 100 ug/kg with headroom (Kabaran 2020 Cyprus n=27 mean 30, max 54; Llorent-Martinez 2014 virgin olive oil below detection).

Cr.label: No government sets a total-chromium maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. This reads across the strictest real food total-chromium ML on the matching liquid, product-as-placed-on-market basis: China GB 2762-2022 total chromium in liquid milk, 300 ug/kg (test method GB 5009.123). Clean commercial olive oil passes (Kabaran 2020 Cyprus n=27 mean 124, max 218; Llorent-Martinez 2014 virgin olive oil below detection); grossly contaminated oil fails. This total-chromium ceiling is the reflex-speciation screen for the hexavalent-chromium control below. GB 2762-2025 supersedes GB 2762-2022 on 2026-09-02; re-verify this value against the 2025 revision at that time.

Cr-VI.label: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. This reads across the strictest drinking-water (oral-intake) Cr(VI) limit as a conservative species ceiling: the California State Water Resources Control Board Cr(VI) MCL, 10 ug/L (about 11 ug/kg at an oil density of 0.91, applied at 10 as slightly conservative). That MCL is a feasibility-set enforceable limit, not a health-based no-effect level (the California Public Health Goal is far lower); it is adopted only as the strictest real sovereign oral-intake Cr(VI) number. The value sits far below the total-chromium screen (300 ug/kg), so the species constraint holds. In a lipid food matrix hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium, so any total-chromium exceedance is reflex-speciated by IC-ICP-MS (EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) and any quantifiable Cr(VI) above 10 ug/kg fails.

Sn.label: No government sets a tin maximum level for an edible oil or fat. The only tin pathway in a bottled oil is migration from tin or tinplate packaging (Charfi 2026 measures 20 ug/kg from a tin container versus 120 ug/kg or below for glass and PET). This reads across the EU Reg 2023/915 inorganic-tin maximum level for canned foods other than beverages, 200000 ug/kg, on the identical product-as-placed-on-market basis: the sovereign instrument purpose-built to bound tin migrating from a metal contact surface into the food it holds. Real oil sits far below it; grossly tin-contaminated oil from failed packaging is caught.

Al.label: No government sets an aluminium maximum level for an edible oil or fat. The demonstrated aluminium pathway in a bottled oil is migration from packaging (Charfi 2026: 670 ug/kg from aluminium containers versus 120 ug/kg or below for glass and PET). This reads across the EU Reg 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration limit, 1000 ug/kg, the sovereign instrument that bounds aluminium migrating into food from a contact material (derived against the EFSA aluminium tolerable weekly intake). The specific-migration limit is applied at face value as a conservative total-content ceiling; the elevated case arose from aluminium metal containers, and the migration limit is disclosed as the nearest sovereign anchor, not direct total-content governance of oil.

tHg.label: government read-across: Thailand MOPH Notification 414 (2020) total mercury 20 for food other than the listed total-mercury categories, the nearest in-force sovereign total-mercury ceiling on the as-sold basis (no government sets a mercury ML for edible oils). Binds once the Israel MoH 2016 guideline row (same value 20, marked not in force by the Ministry 19.02.2026) is gated in the register.

Ni.label: No government sets a nickel maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. This reads across the nearest applicable sovereign nickel ML on the oil's own product-as-placed-on-market (liquid) basis: EU Reg 2024/1987 nickel in infant and young-child formula (liquid form), 100 ug/kg. The more permissive EU fruiting-vegetable nickel ML (400 ug/kg) was rejected because it would admit oil at concentrations reported in contaminated samples. Nickel can also enter a fat as residual hydrogenation catalyst (Raney nickel) in any hardened or partially hydrogenated fraction; this ceiling caps that pathway too. Disclosed as a read-across, not direct EU governance of oil.

Cr.label: No government sets a total-chromium maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. This reads across the strictest real food total-chromium ML on the matching liquid, product-as-placed-on-market basis: China GB 2762-2022 total chromium in liquid milk, 300 ug/kg (test method GB 5009.123). Clean commercial cooking oil sits well below this ceiling; grossly contaminated oil fails. This total-chromium ceiling is the reflex-speciation screen for the hexavalent-chromium control below. GB 2762-2025 supersedes GB 2762-2022 on 2026-09-02; re-verify this value against the 2025 revision at that time.

That MCL is a feasibility-set enforceable limit, not a health-based no-effect level; it is adopted only as the strictest real sovereign oral-intake Cr(VI) number. The value sits far below the total-chromium screen (300 ug/kg), so the species constraint holds. In a lipid food matrix hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium, so any total-chromium exceedance is reflex-speciated by IC-ICP-MS (EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) and any quantifiable Cr(VI) above 10 ug/kg fails.

Sn.label: No government sets a tin maximum level for an edible oil or fat. The only tin pathway in a bottled oil is migration from tin or tinplate packaging. This reads across the EU Reg 2023/915 inorganic-tin maximum level for canned foods other than beverages, 200000 ug/kg, on the identical product-as-placed-on-market basis: the sovereign instrument purpose-built to bound tin migrating from a metal contact surface into the food it holds. Real oil sits far below it; grossly tin-contaminated oil from failed packaging is caught.

Al.label: No government sets an aluminium maximum level for an edible oil or fat. The demonstrated aluminium pathway in a bottled oil is migration from packaging. This reads across the EU Reg 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration limit, 1000 ug/kg, the sovereign instrument that bounds aluminium migrating into food from a contact material (derived against the EFSA aluminium tolerable weekly intake). The specific-migration limit is applied at face value as a conservative total-content ceiling, disclosed as the nearest sovereign anchor, not direct total-content governance of oil.

tHg.label: government read-across: Thailand MOPH Notification 414 (2020) total mercury 20 for food other than the listed total-mercury categories, the nearest in-force sovereign total-mercury ceiling on the as-sold basis (no government sets a mercury ML for edible oils). Binds once the Israel MoH 2016 guideline row (same value 20, marked not in force by the Ministry 19.02.2026) is gated in the register.

_israel_note_2026_09_02: 2026-09-02: M1 verification found the Israel MoH 2016 heavy-metals guideline not in force (gov.il, 19.02.2026; Israel adopted EU 2023/915). tHg re-anchored to Thailand MOPH 414/2020 at the same value 20. Cd (Israel fats-and-oils 0.03 mg/kg) has NO same-value in-force sovereign analog on the as-sold basis: the nearest are EU 2023/915 oilseeds 100 and Uruguay liquid foods 100, a raise from 30 that is held for ratification (OI-20260902-il-fcs2016-not-in-force); the Cd cell keeps the Israel anchor until ratified and is refuted in the confidence manifest meanwhile.
